chapter: Armstrong band memories, Chicago players and Baltimore
title: Stump Whitlock plays Louis's "Shine"
summary: Budd corrects himself that Ellis "Stump" Whitlock, not Stump Evans, was the trumpeter Louis let play 'Shine', including in Louisville.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, the reason he would write these kind of arrangements, you see, Louis sometimes, you know, he would -- he'd take along in the mission, and the rest of the band, we had to play sometimes by ourselves, without Louis. So, we had other music to play, you know. And, Stump Whitlock. That's the guy's name. Not Stump Evans. Stump
Oh, yeah, that's right. Stomp Whitlock.

Stomp Whitlock. Louie really took a liking to little Stomp, and he used to let Stomp sometimes play Shine. You know, that was Louie's feature. And, Stomp would -- would get up and play Shine and try to hit all of the high C's like Louie and end up on the high F. He did a pretty good job with that.

I never will forget, we went to Louisville, Kentucky. That Stomp's home town. And, Louie let Stomp take over quite a bit of things, because Stomp used to listen to Louie and he used to try to copy all his solos. He played pretty good.
